newsitem.title: USA: Calif. unemployment to drop, income to climb - Gov.
newsitem.headline: Calif. unemployment to drop, income to climb - Gov.

text.p: Solid gains in California employment and income were projected to continue for the next two years with state growth above the national average, Gov. Pete Wilson's office said on Thursday.

California's unemployment rate was projected to register 7.3 percent in 1996, decline to 6.8 percent in 1997, then rise to 6.9 percent in 1998, according to Wilson's budget summary for fiscal year 1997-1998.
Personal income growth was expected to remain strong -- increasing by more than 6.5 percent in 1997 and by 6.0 percent in 1998, the budget summary said.
Nonfarm employment was projected to grow faster than the nation for the next two years, Wilson said. The state's economy should create over 300,000 new jobs in 1997, his summary projected.

New home construction should continue its slow recovery, with permits rising from 94,000 units in 1996 to 110,000 in 1997, and 121,000 in 1998, Wilson said. Given low office and industrial vacancy rates, nonresidential construction should continue to increase over the next two years, he said.
Inflation in California was projected to increase slightly, rising from 2.0 percent in 1996 to 2.7 percent in 1997 and 1998, the summary said.
